RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Wednesday, the August 23, 2006/Bhadrapada 1, 1928 (Saka)
————
(Ministries: Commerce and Industry; Defence; Home Affairs; Labour and
Employment; Rural Development; Textiles)
Total number of questions —20
ISI activities in Kashmir Valley
*381. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA:
SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether irrespective of Government's
peace initiative and Prime Minister's
invitation to Kashmiri separatist leaders for
round table conference, ISI refuses to stop
its nefarious activities in valley;
(b) if so, whether according to reports,
ISI is promoting three terrorist outfits and
has directed the commanders of Lashkar-
e-Tayeba and A1-Badar to continue attacks;
(c) whether ISI has increased
remuneration to terrorist outfits as a reward
for their activities;
(d) whether several attacks, bomb
blasts and killing of tourists on 11th July
and earlier are result of such activities;
and
(e) whether this has forced India to
delay proposed ministerial talks with
Pakistan?
Delay in finalisation of
Defence Plans
*382.   SHRI SANTOSH BAGRODIA:
SHRI HARISH RAWAT:
Will the Minister of DEFENCE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
finalisation of 10th Defence Plan was
delayed;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether Government have taken
cognizance of the media reports
apprehending delay in 11th Defence Plan
too;
(d) if so, does Government agree with
media reports;
(e) if so, reasons for the delay;
(f) whether it is a fact that inter-service
rivalry has been one of the causes of delay
in finalising the Defence Plans; and
(g) if so, what steps are being taken to
finalise the Defence Plan in time?

119
Employment in Private Sector
Industries under NREGA
†*383. SHRI DHARAM PAL
SABHARWAL: Will the Minister of
RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that private sector
industries have assured to provide
employment under National Rural
Employment Guarantee Act;
(b) if so, the details thereof; and
(c) the reaction of Government thereto?
Construction of ponds under NREG
Scheme in Gujarat
†*384. DR. MURLI MANOHAR
JOSHI:
SHRI RAJ MOHINDER
SINGH MAJITHA:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that 200 cubic
meter ponds were made in Gujarat through
National Rural Employment Guarantee
Scheme under monitoring of farmers which
created an extra capacity of 2.54 crore cubic
meter water storage;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that due to
this scheme the water problem being faced
by the farmers has been addressed upto
some extent; and
(d) if so, the reaction of Government
thereto and whether Government propose
to contemplate to implement this model at
national level?
Smooth crossing of Wagha
Border
*385. SHRI TARLOCHAN SINGH:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) how many persons crossed Wagha
Border by road during the last two years,
month-wise;
(b) what is the average time taken in
clearance of one person;
(c) what steps are being taken to
strengthen the staff there; and
(d) whether Government would open a
separate line at Wagha for easy flow of
trade?
Increase in naxal activities
†*386. SHRI LALIT KISHORE
CHATURVEDI: Will the Minister of
HOME AFFAIRS be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that naxalite
activities have increased in forests areas of
naxal affected States Jharkhand,
Chhattisgarh, Orissa, Andhra Pradesh,
Bihar and Madhya Pradesh since the year
2003;
(b) whether coordinated and integrated
efforts to check the said activities in naxal
affected States could not be made due to
the lenient attitude of Central Government
and some State Governments towards
them; and
(c) whether any intense campaign to
get rid of the said problem is under
consideration of Government; if not, the
reasons therefor?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

120
Threat to Kashmiri Pandits by
Terrorists in Valley
*387. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
SHRI SURENDRA LATH:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Kashmiri
Pandits have been forced to declare
performance of ‘Mahashradh’ in Jammu
instead of valley in view of threats from
terrorists; and
(b) if so, whether Government will
ensure that they are able to return to
valley at least for such acts?
Compensation to farmers for laying
mines
*388. SHRI T. S. BAJWA: Will the
Minister of DEFENCE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether full and final compensation
have since been paid to all the eligible
farmers whose lands were used for laying
mines etc. by the army on the Indo-Pak
border in J&K especially in Ranbir Singh
Pura Sector;
(b) whether any claims are still
pending; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Rural Development Fund
†*389. SHRI KRISHAN LAL
BALMIKI: Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are going to
create a Rural Development Fund; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the
manner in which Government would
mobilize financial resources for this
purpose?
Unfair treatment to Virginia tobacco
at WTO negotiations
*390. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND  INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have noted
that cash crops like Virginia tobacco are
not receiving fair treatment during WTO
negotiations;
(b) whether it is also a fact that Free
Trade Agreements between India and
neighbouring countries is harming Indian
tobacco farmers' interests;
(c) in what way will Government bring
about equity and fairness in international
trade policies to help farmers of Andhra
Pradesh and Karnataka; and
(d) the steps proposed to review such
aspects of FTAs which harm Indian
farmers?
DNA finger printing certificate for
Basmati rice export
†*391. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA:
MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether European Commission has
imposed a condition of DNA finger
printing  certification from 1st July, 2006
for exemption of 42.5 Euro per tonne in
respect of custom duty on Basmati
rice;
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

121
(b) whether the Indian exporters of
Basmati rice will have to attach a DNA
finger printing certificate with each
consignment of rice;
(c) whether they would have to contact
the Export Inspection Council and the
Centre for DNA finger printing,
Hyderabad to get that certificate; and
(d) if so, arrangement being made by
Government for that so that small
exporters do not face unnecessary
hardships in getting the same?
Housing problem in the country
†*392. PROF. ALKA BALRAM
KSHATRIYA: Will the Minister of
RURAL DEVELOPMENT be pleased to
state:
(a) whether Government are making
any efforts to tackle the housing problem
at rural and urban levels in the country;
(b) if so, the number of houses
constructed under the different schemes
during the last three years and State-wise
details of the houses allocated to poor and
backward people of different communities;
(c) whether Government would be able
to solve the housing problem by the end
of the year 2015; and
(d) if so, the number of houses targeted
to be constructed every year?
Conversion of agricultural land for
commercial activities
*393. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the large scale conversion
of agricultural land to set up business
Centres, Malls, amusement parks, etc.,
affecting the food production in the
country;
(b) whether it is a fact that in most of
such deals, the peasants are paid less
than the market value of the land; and
(c) if the answer to parts (a) & (b)
above be in the affirmative, the details in
this regard and Government's reaction
thereto?
Setting up of Human Trafficking
Control Boards in States
*394.SHRIMATI HEMA MALINI:
Will the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS
be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are aware that
the Apex Court asked to set up Human
Trafficking Control Board in every State
for better coordination and making
provision of compensation and
rehabilitation of the victims;
(b) if so, what is the reaction of
Government and what sort of
compensation and rehabilitation have been
provided to the victims so far; and
(c) the details thereof and the number
of victims?
Export of sugar
†*395. MS. SUSHILA TIRIYA:
SHRI MOTILAL VORA:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND  INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the quantum of sugar exported in
the year 2005-06 alongwith the names of
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

122
countries and at which rate this export
was made;
(b) the target fixed for the export of
sugar in the year  2006-07 and the details
of countries to which the same is to be
exported; and
(c) the share of STC in the total
quantities of sugar to be exported and
reasons for lesser share given therein to
the STC?
Anti-terrorism technology from
Israel
*396. SHRI SHAHID SIDDIQUI: Will
the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government are planning
to buy or borrow technology from Israel
to counter terrorism; and
(b) whether the Ministry is taking
help of Israel to counter or fight terrorism
in India, if so, what are the areas of this
co-operation?
Relief package for handloom
co-operatives
*397. SHRIMATI S. G. INDIRA :
Will the Minister of TEXTILES be pleased
to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
are considering a Rs. 1000 crore debt
relief package for handloom cooperatives;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether it is also a fact that
Government are considering to extend the
Technology Upgradation Fund Scheme to
the handloom sector; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
National Food for Work Programme
*398. SHRI RAMDAS AGARWAL:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the year-wise and State-wise
allocation of funds and quantum of
foodgrains supplied under the National
Food for Work Programme (NFFWP) in
the last five years, till date;
(b) whether Government have received
any requests from certain States, including
drought-prone States, for additional
amount as well as foodgrains during the
said period; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and the
action taken thereon, State-wise?
Assault on students of Jamia Millia
Islamia University
*399. SHRI KAMAL AKHTAR: Will
the Minister of HOME AFFAIRS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government's attention has
been drawn to the University authorities
sponsored brutal assault on students of
Jamia Millia Islamia University;
(b) whether Government are going to
accept the version of the authorities
responsible for the alleged assault, for
enquiry by their hand picked person, or
are going to conduct an impartial
investigation; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and if not,
the reasons therefor?

123
Amending existing labour laws
*400. SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL: Will the Minister of
LABOUR AND EMPLOYMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether there is any move to
amend the existing labour laws;

List of Questions for WRITTEN  ANSWERS

————
(Ministries: Commerce and Industry; Defence; Home Affairs; Labour and
Employment; Rural Development; Textiles)
Total number of questions —155
Private promoters in SEZs
2724. MS. MABEL REBELLO: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) how many private promoters are in
Special Economic Zones;
(b) their names and areas where they
are developers;
(c) how much land each of them have
acquired in each Zone and per acre paid by
them; and
(d) at what price will they be selling
land to entrepreneurs in these zones?
Pending proposals for
Industrialization in Tamil Nadu
2725. SHRI N.R. GOVINDARAJAR:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the proposals pending before
Government for industrialisation, trade
promotion and setting up of new industries
for over all economic development of  Tamil
Nadu; and
(b) by when these proposals are likely
to be approved?
Import export with Bangladesh and
vice versa
2726. SHRI MATILAL SARKAR: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the names of items which are
imported to India from Bangladesh and
those which are exported from India to
Bangladesh as per trade agreement between
the two countries;
(b) which of those items have been
settled up by the present Government;
(c) whether Government have been
contemplating setting up open markets at
the border, for the benefit of the local
producers and to dilute the smuggling
tendency among some sections of traders;
(d) if so, the details of the programme
in that regard; and

630
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Impact of FDI on agriculture and
plantation
2727. SHRI TARIQ ANWAR: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that Government
have taken a decision to allow FDI upto
100 per cent in agriculture/plantation
activities;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government have taken into
consideration the fact that if FDI is
permitted, the prices of agricultural products
would not be controllable; and
(d) the other consequence which the
people of India would have to face due to
this?
Doubling the trade between India and
Thailand
2728. SHRIMATI SYEDA ANWARA
TAIMUR: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that India and
Thailand are exploring opportunities to
double the annual trade to 4 billion dollar in
the next couple of years, and expand the
list of items that could be traded, from 82
to about 5,000;
(b) whether a working group from
Thailand had discussions with the
concerned officials here to double the trade
volume from two billion dollar to four
billion dollar; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Import of vanaspati from Sri Lanka
2729. SHRI P.R. RAJAN: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether import of vanaspati from
Sri Lanka is duty free under the Free Trade
Agreement ;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether there is any policy for
controlling, regulating and for proper
distribution of the imported vanaspati;
(d) if so, whether NAFED is associated
with the above distribution;
(e) whether the Directorate of
Vanaspati, Vegetable Oils and Fats has
recommended fixation of Tariff rate Quota
(TRQ) for duty free import of Vanaspati;
(f) if so, the action taken on above
recommendation; and
(g) the steps taken to protect the
domestic vanaspati industry from the
impact of the duty free import?
Certification for arecanut import by
CPCRI
2730. SHRI A. VIJAYARAGHAVAN:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Central Plantation
Crops Research Institute (CPCRI) has
certified during 2006 that the arecanut
imported are of inferior quality;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether there is any regulatory body
to control arecanut import and check its
quality; and
(d) if so, the details thereof and if not,
whether steps would be taken to constitute
such a body?

631
China-India trade
2731. PROF. P.J. KURIEN: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that China-India
trade will surpass the target of $20 billion
before the financial year 2008;
(b) whether it is a fact that a vast portion
of exports from India consist of raw
materials like iron ore, etc;
(c) what steps would be taken by
Government to encourage and help change
the profile of our exports to China; and
(d) the steps proposed to involve the
industry and various institutions, to come
up with solutions to improve the quality
and value of our exports to China?
Funds for industrial development of
Uttaranchal
2732. SHRI HARISH RAWAT: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the details of funds allocated for
industrial development for hilly and
backward areas of Uttaranchal during the
10th Five Year Plan period;
(b) the amount released to the State so
far, since 2002 to date, year-wise;
(c) whether the State has fully utilized
the released amount;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) if not, the reasons therefor?
Board for development and export of
fisheries
2733. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether a Board for development
and export of fisheries is being planned;
(b) if so, what would be the plans for
Andhra Pradesh with a very long sea coast
and large number of inland fishery sources;
and
(c) whether Government would
consider setting up the Board’s office in
Andhra Pradesh?
Reduction in consumption of Coffee
2734. SHRIMATI PREMA
CARIAPPA: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the
consumption of Coffee in the country has
remained stagnant for several decades;
(b) if so, what steps have been taken by
Government during the last three years to
promote the consumption of Coffee within
the country; and
(c) what are the plans of Government
to develop the domestic market for Coffee?
Resolution of issues in the WTO
2735. SHRI LALIT SURI: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether India withdrew from the
mini ministerial level conference of WTO
held recently in Geneva;
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) whether any efforts are being made
by various interests to come to a
compromise on the issues, concerning the
developed and the developing countries;
and
(d) if so, the details thereof?

632
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Industrial backward areas in
Rajasthan
2736. DR. GYAN PRAKASH
PILANIA: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have identified
'industrial backward areas', in Rajasthan;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether Government propose to
formulate any action plan for the
development of such backward areas;
(d) if so, the details thereof; and
(e) what specific steps are being taken
by Government for their development?
Export of iron-ore by MMTC
†2737. SHRI AJAY MAROO: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the public
sector company MMTC exports around
four crore ton iron-ore every year;
(b) whether the MMTC exports at the
rate of 44 dollar per ton, whereas iron-ore's
cost in the open market is 54 dollar per
ton;
(c) if so, the reasons therefor; and
(d) if not, the actual position in this
regard?
Pending proposals for AEZs
2738. SHRI C.
RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) the number of proposal for setting
up of Agri-Export Zones pending with
Government at present, State-wise,
particularly from Andhra Pradesh;
(b) the reasons for the delay in clearing
the same; and
(c) by when the same is likely to be
cleared, State-wise?
Consumption and export of iron ore
2739. SHRI GIREESH KUMAR
SANGHI:
SHRI JAI PARKASH
AGGARWAL:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) what has been the volume of export
of iron ore during the last five years;
(b) what are the future export
commitments in this regard;
(c) what have been the per tonne net
earnings over these exports;
(d) what are the total proven reserves
of iron ore in the country; and
(e) what have been the domestic
consumption levels of iron ore during the
last three years and what are the future
projections?
Registered units in EOUs and SEZs
2740. SHRI V. HANUMANTHA
RAO: Will the Minister of COMMERCE
AND INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government have
organized open house meetings for EOUs
and SEZ units, which are registered, under
the auspices of Export Promotion
Councils;
(b) how many such EOUs and SEZ units
are actually registered with the appropriate
authorities of Government;

633
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(c) of these how many are actually
working;
(d) whether it is a fact that many units
are only operating to avail the fiscal
benefits; and
(e) the steps proposed to de-register
such units?
Protection of Green belt in approving
SEZ around Delhi
2741. SHRI TARLOCHAN SINGH:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that there are
some conflicting provisions in the SEZ Act
such as power to land use change in
Haryana in contravention of the fact that
under the National Capital Region Act a
Regional Plan has been approved;
(b) whether the SEZ will deprive the
Green belt being envisaged around Delhi
under Regional Plan; and
(c) how Government propose to
safeguards the interest of Capital while
approving any SEZ around Delhi?
Revision of North East Industrial
Policy
2742. SHRI VIJAY J. DARDA: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government propose to
revise the North East Industrial Policy;
(b) if so, by when; and
(c) the names of the industries which
are likely to benefit from the new policy?
Closure of cinchona plantation
†2743. SHRI SAMAN PATHAK: Will
the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that a number of
cinchona plantations in the country are on
the verge of closure due to less consumption
of this medicinal plant within the country
as well as abroad;
(b) the number of cinchona plantations
in the country and the details thereof;
(c) the present condition of cinchona
plantations of Darjeeling and whether
Government have any scheme for revival
of cinchona industry; and
(d) if so, the details thereof?
Decline in Indo-Myanmar border
trade
2744. SHRI EKANATH K. THAKUR:
Will the Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Indo-
Myanmar border trade through Moreh is
down from Rs. 57.53 crore in 1997-98 to a
dismal Rs. 5.48 crore in 2000-01, and to
Rs. 10.65 crore in 2004-05;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
illegal border trade is nine times the legal
trade;
(c) if so, whether Government have
made any investigations in this matter; and
(d) the steps Government propose to
take to conduct trade through mutually
agreed system of freely convertible
currencies?

634
Doubling of Indo-US bilateral trade
2745. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether India and the US have agreed
to set up initiative to double bilateral trade
to  $50 billion over next three years;
(b) whether any action plan was
discussed by the Commerce Minister
with the US trade representative, in June,
2006;
(c) if so, whether the plan includes
infrastructure investment programme, that
would give India opportunities, incentives
and challenges in power, roads, ports and
airports;
(d) whether both the countries have
asked one another to life barriers, to
push two-way trade in goods and
services; and
(e) if so, to what extent both India and
US have taken decisions in this regard?
MNF status to India by Pakistan
2746. SHRI B.J. PANDA: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) what is the position regarding grant
of Most Favoured Nation (MNF) status
by Pakistan to India, after ratification of
South Asia Free Trade Agreement
(SAFTA);
(b) whether Pakistan has put forward
certain pre-conditions, before grant of
MNF status of India; and
(c) if so, the details thereof?
Revival of closed plantations in
Kerala
2747. SHRI K.E. ISMAIL: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether the Kerala Government has
submitted any proposal for revival of the
closed plantations, if so the details thereof
and the response of the Central
Government thereto;
(b) whether Government are aware that
Managements of some of these closed
plantations are selling the movable
properties, cutting of trees and selling the
same, and even demolishing buildings and
selling them, while they do nothing to revive
the plantations nor help the starving
workers; and
(c) whether Government would
consider proposal of the Trade Unions
expressing their willingness to take over
and run plantations, provided Government
extend support to them?
Economic cooperation between India
and Pakistan
2748. SHRI C.
RAMACHANDRAIAH: Will the
Minister of COMMERCE AND
INDUSTRY be pleased to state:
(a) whether India and Pakistan have
decided to set up a Joint Parliamentary
Group on Economic Cooperation between
the two countries;
(b) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken thereon;
(c) to what extent this group would help
to improve Economic Cooperation between
the two countries;

635
(d) whether Pakistan has also decided
to open land route for trading selected
commodities, including live animals; and
(e) if so, the details thereof, the items
exported to Pakistan so far, and those likely
to be exported?
Easy import of sugar, pulses and wheat
2749. SHRIMATI SHOBHANA
BHARTIA: Will the Minister of
COMMERCE AND INDUSTRY be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the rise in prices of essential
commodities has compelled Government to
facilitate easy import of sugar, pulses and
wheat in a bid to keep prices under check;
(b) if so, whether Government are
planning to institute a tariff quota regime,
to facilitate import of sugar against lower
duty, eliminate import duty on pulses and
enable easy import of wheat;
